transcript.text: Stop tilling your soil every spring! Here are three common soil mistakes gardeners make before planting tomatoes. Mistake one: digging too deep and disrupting mycorrhizal fungal networks. Mistake two: using fresh animal manure that burns delicate feeder roots. Mistake three: guessing your soil pH without a simple litmus test. Save your soil biology this season!

generated_content.title: 3 Signs Your Soil Is Starving For Organic Matter
generated_content.hook: If your garden soil feels like concrete after it rains, your soil biology is starving.
generated_content.script: If your garden soil feels like concrete after it rains, your soil biology is starving. Here are three unmistakable signs your soil needs living organic matter right now. First: water pooling on the surface instead of absorbing like a sponge. That means your soil has lost its crumb structure. Second: zero earthworm activity when you dig down four inches. Earthworms are nature's soil aerators. And third: pale, stunted seedling growth despite regular watering. Don't reach for synthetic quick fixes that scorch the soil microbiome. Instead, top-dress with two inches of well-aged compost and let soil organisms do the heavy lifting. Follow Organic Journals for weekly regenerative soil guides.
